correctness.rationale: The exact finite shelling_orders.json contains a complete permutation of the disconnected-triple facet set at each of n=21..26. A separate checker recomputes graph triples and checks for every new facet and every earlier facet the pure-shelling ridge-intersection condition; verified facet counts are 805,990,1196,1424,1675,1950 and spanning counts 1,12,24,37,51,66. The same checker exhaustively constructs Alexander-dual simplices for each n=13..20, reduces all augmented boundary matrices over F2, and finds lower-degree homology obstruction; the n<=12 void statement has an elementary nonneighbor proof. For n>=27 an actual theorem, Chauhan--Shukla Theorem 1.4, supplies the infinite positive tail with exactly the same wedge ranks. No infinite claim is extrapolated from finite code. The shelling criterion equivalence is reconstructed in RESULT.md. Independent validation not performed.

value.rationale: Conjecture 4.2(ii) poses a natural all-power shellability transition with connections to Stanley--Reisner Cohen--Macaulayness. This settles its entire next nontrivial fixed fifth-power case rather than a random slice: six previously uncovered positive orders complete the sharp all-size classification. Shellability is strictly stronger than knowing earlier tabulated homology ranks and gives integral wedge homotopy types. The finite certificates are complete and reusable, while the published large-order theorem handles the unbounded tail. The claim is not the known rank formula alone.
